name: TRIGA stainless-clad U-ZrH (H/Zr 1.6): fuel temperature limits
label: sourced
description: The fuel temperature limit of TRIGA fuel with stainless steel cladding and U-ZrH at a hydrogen to zirconium ratio of about 1.6: 1150 C while the cladding is at most 500 C, and 950 C once the cladding is above 500 C (the cladding loses yield strength above 500 C, so the hydrogen pressure that fuel temperature makes would stress it). The limit comes from hydrogen outgassing and the clad stress it produces; FEED computes neither, it only compares the temperature. It does not cover aluminium cladding, a different hydrogen ratio, or any other failure mechanism. At exactly 500 C of cladding the 1150 C rule applies (at most 500).
citation: Kansas State University TRIGA Mark II Safety Analysis Report, Dec 2004, section 3.5.1 (Fuel System) and section 4.7 (Safety Limit), citing NUREG-1282: 1150 C with clad < 500 C and 950 C with clad > 500 C for U-ZrH (H/Zr 1.65). University of Texas at Austin TRIGA II Safety Analysis Report (redacted), Ch. 4 section 4.2.1: the same two values from the hoop stress against the stainless-steel strength (Figures 4.3a, 4.3b), and pulsing of fuel with H/Zr of at least 1.65 to about 1150 C without damage to the cladding (General Atomics report GACD 6977).

name: TRIGA stainless-clad U-ZrH (H/Zr 1.6): fuel limits for steady operation (750 C design limit and the two safety limits)
label: sourced
description: For a steady-state case: the 750 C operational design limit on the fuel temperature, then the two safety limits of the other set (1150 C while the cladding is at most 500 C, 950 C once it is above). General Atomics gives the 750 C as a design basis for steady operation, chosen because at the resulting average fuel temperatures the fuel growth from irradiation and fission products is insignificant; it is a design limit, not a point of failure, and a pulse goes above it by design, so do not use this set for a pulse (use the safety-limit set). The two safety limits come from hydrogen outgassing and the cladding stress it produces; FEED computes neither, it only compares the temperature. This set does not cover aluminium cladding, a different hydrogen ratio, burnup (the growth limit assumes the fuel burnt in a normal TRIGA core) or any other failure mechanism.
citation: M. T. Simnad, The U-ZrHx Alloy: Its Properties and Use in TRIGA Fuel, General Atomic report E-117-833 (GA Project No. 4314), chapter 4: a steady-state operational fuel temperature design limit of 750 C based on irradiation- and fission-product-induced fuel growth and deformation; the pulsing safety limit of 1150 C for stainless-steel U-ZrH1.65 while the cladding is below 500 C (pages 4-1 to 4-3 and 4-6 to 4-7), and 950 C where the cladding can be as hot as the fuel (the equilibrium hydrogen pressure then equals the cladding's ultimate strength). The K-State SAR (Dec 2004, sections 3.5.1 and 4.7, citing NUREG-1282) and the UT-Austin SAR (Ch. 4 section 4.2.1) give the same 1150 C and 950 C.
